_comment: Answer quality. Milestone 4.
DIFFERENT AXIS FROM MILESTONE 3. M3 asked 'is it true?'. M4 asks 'is it a
good answer?'. An answer can be perfectly grounded and still be a poor
answer: it can miss half the question, volunteer facts nobody asked for,
skip its citations, or bury one sentence of content in a page of prose.
HOW EACH DIMENSION IS MADE DETERMINISTIC:
required_parts    the distinct things the question asks for. Each part
lists alternative strings that count as answering it,
because the model paraphrases freely. COMPLETENESS is
the fraction of parts covered.
off_topic_facts   facts that ARE in the corpus but are NOT what this
question asked for. This is the whole trick of
measuring PRECISION without a judge: if one of these
appears, the model over-answered. They are real facts,
so M3 would score them as perfectly grounded.
expect_citation   whether a factual claim here should carry [Chunk #N].
max_words         a hand-set ceiling for a direct answer to THIS
question, sized to the number of parts. CONCISENESS
degrades past it rather than failing at a cliff.
CASE DESIGN — deliberately mixed so the suite can discriminate:
AQ-01..03   single-part, tight budget. Baseline.
AQ-04..06   OVER-ANSWERING TRAPS. The source document holds several
facts; only one was asked for. GND-04 in milestone 3 showed
the model doing exactly this and scoring 1.00.
AQ-07..09   MULTI-PART. Two or three things asked at once; completeness
is the point.
AQ-10..12   cross-document and precision-under-pressure.
Every fact below was read from eval/corpus_retrieval/*.md by hand. No fact
is invented, including the off-topic ones.

questions.question: How many digits is the OTP?
questions.note: single fact, but 02-otp-delivery.md holds three others. Tight budget.

questions.question: What is the minimum password length?
questions.note: OVER-ANSWER TRAP. In milestone 3 this exact document produced an answer covering length, classes, masking AND max length — all grounded, none asked for.

questions.question: How long is the lockout period?
questions.note: single fact; the threshold is the tempting extra

questions.question: What is the retention period for audit entries?
questions.note: OVER-ANSWER TRAP. 'Who can read them' is the natural companion fact and was NOT asked.

questions.question: What is the session idle timeout?
questions.note: OVER-ANSWER TRAP. 06-session-handling.md has four facts; one was asked for.

questions.question: Where do field errors appear on the page?
questions.note: OVER-ANSWER TRAP. Styling is the obvious thing to volunteer.

questions.question: How many digits is the OTP, and how long is it valid for?
questions.note: MULTI-PART, two parts. Same source document as AQ-01 — the difference is that the second fact is now REQUIRED rather than off-topic.

questions.question: How many failed attempts trigger a lockout, how long does it last, and what resets the counter?
questions.note: MULTI-PART, three parts. Tests whether the third part gets dropped.

questions.question: What are the password character requirements, and is there an upper limit on length?
questions.note: MULTI-PART. Minimum length is intentionally NOT required here and NOT off-topic — it sits adjacent to both parts, so penalising it would be unfair.

questions.question: What happens to a session token when a user logs out, and what status is returned if it is replayed?
questions.note: MULTI-PART within one document, with two in-document distractors

questions.question: What does the Forgot Password link do?
questions.note: single part; 05-navigation.md holds three other navigation facts

questions.question: What is the exact error message for a mobile number that is too short, and what is the field's maxlength?
questions.note: MULTI-PART, one exact string plus one technical attribute
